name: Quebec Jean Lesage International Airport
before:
Quebec City's airport, 17 km west of the centre in the Sainte-Foy borough, and the eleventh busiest in Canada with just over 1.8 million passengers in 2025.

The route map is wider than the size suggests. More than ten airlines run hundreds of weekly flights to destinations across Canada and the United States and out to Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean and Europe, so a client does not automatically have to connect through Montreal.

The main terminal has seventeen gates, numbered from 20 to 37, and twelve of them have an air bridge, which is a better ratio than many airports this size.

Two runways serve it, the main one at 9,000 feet and a shorter second at 5,700 feet, with seven taxiways between them. A third apron handles general aviation, charter operators, flight schools and maintenance work.

It is named after Jean Lesage, and is designated an international airport by Transport Canada.
after:
Quebec City's airport, 17 km west of the centre in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough, with about 1.8 million passengers in 2025.

The route map is wider than the size suggests. More than ten airlines fly from here, and the airport lists direct flights to more than 30 destinations. They reach across Canada and the United States and out to Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean and Europe, so a client does not automatically have to connect through Montreal.

Two runways serve it, the main one at 9,000 feet and a shorter second at 5,700 feet.

It is named after Jean Lesage.

claims.wasBefore: and the eleventh busiest in Canada
claims.why: Cannot be confirmed. Statistics Canada's 2025 table puts Québec eleventh among airports with a published figure (1,764,289, behind Kelowna and Victoria), but Toronto Billy Bishop's figure is suppressed for 2024 and 2025, and in 2023, the last year both were published, Billy Bishop had 2,000,714 against Québec's 1,656,028. So Québec may be twelfth.

claims.claim: no US preclearance at Québec City
claims.why: Held back: a fact the old text never mentioned. Preclearance was announced for Québec City in 2016 and again in 2019, but Wikipedia says it was not yet available as of March 2024, and CBP's list (modified 24 June 2026) still has no Québec City site among its ten Canadian locations. So clients to the US clear US border checks on arrival, unlike at Montreal or Ottawa. Worth adding if Andy wants it.
